question: Does the revised PAREX EIS provide dated, station-resolved fish evidence along the Pasig River corridor that can be crosswalked to NCR and nearby Rizal without overstating its scope?
citation: RHR Consulting Services, Inc. (2022). Environmental Impact Assessment: Pasig River Expressway Project (Revised EIS Report), prepared for SMC Infrastructure. Official copy hosted on the DENR Environmental Management Bureau EIA portal.

sourceAccess.cover: The cover identifies the Pasig River Expressway Project, SMC Infrastructure as the client, RHR Consulting Services, Inc. as preparer, and 2022 as the year.
sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the public EMB-hosted PDF text view on 2026-11-19. No PDF copy, table image, fish photograph, or raw field data was downloaded or retained.
sourceLocators: Freshwater ecology overview and Table 2-16, report pages 2-97 to 2-98: six stations, localities, coordinates, depth, flow and survey date.
Figure 2-51, report page 2-99: freshwater ecology sampling-map context.
Fish method and Table 2-19, report pages 2-108 to 2-109: hook-and-line collection and station presence matrix.
Table 2-20 and surrounding text, report pages 2-110 to 2-111: separate taxonomic table and report's 14-species summary.

fieldSurvey.scopeAsReported: Freshwater ecology assessment along the proposed project alignment, covering six sampling points in Manila, Mandaluyong, Makati, Pasig, and Taytay, Rizal.
fieldSurvey.fishMethodAsReported: Fish samples were collected through fishing lines by fisherfolk within the sampling area. Each site was fished for 30 minutes; collected fish were taken to a laboratory for identification using cited fish references and FishBase validation.
fieldSurvey.dateAsReported: 2021-10-07 for each of the six freshwater-ecology stations in Table 2-16. The review does not infer additional or repeated sampling dates.
fieldSurvey.habitatScope: The report labels this section freshwater ecology. It does not provide station salinity or a fish-specific freshwater/brackish classification; FWE 1 is mapped near Manila Bay and FWE 6 is at the Taytay, Rizal end of the reported corridor. Keep habitat transition and exact terminal watercourse identity unresolved.

fishMatrix.table: Table 2-19, The ichthyofauna presence on the six sampling stations along the alignment of the proposed project.

higherTaxonRow.interpretation: Higher taxon row; not a species-level record.

fishMatrix.absenceMeaning: The source's '-' cells are outcomes of this single reported survey event at the listed stations; they are not evidence of ecological absence or current absence.

tableReconciliation.reportedTotal: The narrative following Table 2-20 states that 14 fish species were observed.

nameSpellingConflict.decision: Preserve both source spellings; do not merge or resolve them in this review.

tableReconciliation.decision: The station matrix and separate taxonomic description are not a reconciled species-by-station dataset. No row is admitted as a public assertion.

regionalCrosswalk.calabarzonStationLocality: Taytay, Rizal (FWE 6 as labeled by the EIS)
regionalCrosswalk.sharedWaterInterpretation: The source presents the survey along a Pasig River project corridor and labels its easternmost station Taytay, Rizal. Link the source review to both NCR and CALABARZON, but do not assign FWE 6 to a named river, floodway, estuary, or lake polygon without a separate crosswalk.
regionalCrosswalk.geometryDecision: No station point or source map geometry was added to an app layer. The printed sample coordinates remain research-only and do not define fishing spots or waterbody extents.

rightsAndEvidenceDecision.decision: Keep the report as an attributed research-only discovery source. Public hosting on the EMB portal does not establish permission to redistribute tables, photos, coordinates, or a normalized derived dataset.

limits: This is a project-focused 2021 snapshot described in a 2022 revised EIS, not a systematic or current Pasig River inventory.

The report describes fisherfolk hook-and-line collection for 30 minutes per site but does not identify voucher specimens, collection catalog numbers, sequences, or an independent verification record in the reviewed pages.
The report's 14-species narrative, 13-row station matrix, and non-matching 13-row taxonomic table remain internally inconsistent.
Station FWE 6 is source-labeled Taytay, Rizal. Its watercourse identity and its relation to the Pasig corridor are not independently crosswalked here.
No present-day occurrence, population trend, water quality or safety clearance, fishing access, or legal catchability statement follows from this source.
nextActions: Keep this source as a held cross-region research lead; search for independently identifiable vouchers, raw station field records, or a corrected survey table before any species-level projection.
Continue the NCR inventory across other freshwater, brackish, tidal, and marine contexts, including source-derived site scope beyond the project corridor.
Reconcile FWE 6 with source-named waterway records without transferring the station coordinate to an entire river, floodway, or lake.
